"'''Rockstar'''" (stylized in [[all caps]]) is a song by American rapper [[DaBaby]], featuring fellow American rapper [[Roddy Ricch]]. The song was released on April 17, 2020, as the second single from DaBaby's third studio album ''[[Blame It on Baby]]'' (2020). It was written by the two rappers. "Rockstar" spent seven non-consecutive weeks at the top of the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|date=June 29, 2020|title=DaBaby's "Rockstar" Tops Hot 100 For 3rd Week|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/business/chart-beat/9411108/dababy-rockstar-number-one-hot-100-third-week|access-date=June 29, 2020|magazine=Billboard}}</ref> Outside of the United States, "Rockstar" topped the charts in Australia, Austria, Canada, Denmark, Greece, New Zealand, Portugal, the Republic of Ireland, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom, and peaked within the top ten of the charts in Belgium, Germany, the Netherlands, France, Norway, Sweden, and Finland. Its music video is set in a [[zombie apocalypse]].

On June 12, 2020, DaBaby released a "[[Black Lives Matter|BLM (Black Lives Matter)]] remix" of "Rockstar", which replaces the intro with an extra verse from him, before the rest of the song, regarding the [[George Floyd protests]] that started in May 2020, and his own experience with [[Police brutality|police abuse]].<ref name="remix">{{Cite web|title=DaBaby Releases "Rockstar (BLM Remix)" Featuring Roddy Ricch|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2020/06/dababy-roddy-ricch-rockstar-blm-remix|access-date=June 12, 2020|website=Complex|language=en}}</ref> The song received nominations for [[Grammy Award for Record of the Year|Record of the Year]], [[Grammy Award for Best Melodic Rap Performance|Best Melodic Rap Performance]], and [[Grammy Award for Best Rap Song|Best Rap Song]] at the [[63rd Annual Grammy Awards]].<ref name=grammy2021>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/11/24/arts/music/grammy-nominees-list.html|title=Grammy Nominations 2021: See the List|work=The New York Times|date=November 24, 2020}}</ref>

"Rockstar" (stylized in all caps) is a song by American rapper DaBaby, featuring fellow American rapper Roddy Ricch. The song was released on April 17, 2020, as the second single from DaBaby's third studio album Blame It on Baby (2020). It was written by the two rappers. "Rockstar" spent seven non-consecutive weeks at the top of the Billboard Hot 100. Outside of the United States, "Rockstar" topped the charts in Australia, Austria, Canada, Denmark, Greece, New Zealand, Portugal, the Republic of Ireland, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom, and peaked within the top ten of the charts in Belgium, Germany, the Netherlands, France, Norway, Sweden, and Finland. Its music video is set in a zombie apocalypse.

On June 12, 2020, DaBaby released a "BLM (Black Lives Matter) remix" of "Rockstar", which replaces the intro with an extra verse from him, before the rest of the song, regarding the George Floyd protests that started in May 2020, and his own experience with police abuse. The song received nominations for Record of the Year, Best Melodic Rap Performance, and Best Rap Song at the 63rd Annual Grammy Awards.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Reviewing the song's predecessor album for ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'', Sam Hockley-Smith found "Rockstar" and "[[Find My Way (DaBaby song)|Find My Way]]" "catchy and brooding", "allowing him [DaBaby] to rehash harrowing moments of violence, inner turmoil, and [[Posttraumatic stress disorder|PTSD]]."<ref name="EW">{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/music/music-reviews/dababy-blame-it-on-baby-review/|title=DaBaby charts a new path forward on Blame It on Baby|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|last=Hockley-Smith |first=Sam|date=April 20, 2020|access-date=April 23, 2020}}</ref> In ''[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]'', Dani Blum noticed DaBaby "doesn't imitate Roddy Ricch as much as adjust his tone to complement the feature," thus, "his voice becomes softer, as close as DaBaby gets to tender, as he talks about the physical jolt of PTSD."<ref name="PF">{{cite web|url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/dababy-blame-it-on-baby/|title=DaBaby Blame It on Baby|work=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]|last=Blum|first=Dani|date=April 21, 2020|access-date=April 21, 2020}}</ref>
sections.text: Reviewing the song's predecessor album for Entertainment Weekly, Sam Hockley-Smith found "Rockstar" and "Find My Way" "catchy and brooding", "allowing him [DaBaby] to rehash harrowing moments of violence, inner turmoil, and PTSD." In Pitchfork, Dani Blum noticed DaBaby "doesn't imitate Roddy Ricch as much as adjust his tone to complement the feature," thus, "his voice becomes softer, as close as DaBaby gets to tender, as he talks about the physical jolt of PTSD."

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext: "Rockstar" reached number one on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] in its seventh week, for the chart issue dated June 13, 2020. It became DaBaby's first chart-topper and Roddy Ricch's second. It also became DaBaby's first number one and Ricch's second on [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs]] and [[Hot Rap Songs]] charts. Along with "[[The Box (Roddy Ricch song)|The Box]]", Ricch became the first artist to achieve his first two number one singles in the same year since [[Ed Sheeran]] did it in 2017.<ref name="number one">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/business/chart-beat/9398276/da-baby-rockstar-number-one-hot-100|title=DaBaby & Roddy Ricch's 'Rockstar' Rises to No. 1 on Billboard Hot 100|magazine=Billboard|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=June 8, 2020|access-date=June 9, 2020}}</ref> Topping the chart for a second week, it became the first single to spend multiple weeks on top after a run in which five songs each spent a first and only week at the summit.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/business/chart-beat/9402603/dababy-rockstar-number-one-second-week-hot-100|title=DaBaby & Roddy Ricch's 'Rockstar' Rules Hot 100 for 2nd Week, Justin Bieber & Quavo's 'Intentions' Hits Top 5|magazine=Billboard|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=June 15, 2020|access-date=June 16, 2020}}</ref> It spent seven non-consecutive weeks atop the chart. "Rockstar" also spent six weeks at number one in both Australia and the United Kingdom,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ariacharts.com.au/news/2020/six-weeks-at-1-for-dababy-s-rockstar|title=Six Weeks at Number One for DaBaby's Rockstar|work=ARIA Charts}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/dababys-rockstar-claims-sixth-week-at-number-1-on-official-singles-chart__30080/|title=DaBaby's Rockstar claims sixth week at Number 1 on Official Singles Chart|work=Official Charts}}</ref> and eight weeks at the top in the Republic of Ireland.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/dababy-s-rockstar-rocks-up-at-number-1-on-the-official-irish-singles-chart-for-an-eighth-week__30194/|title=DaBaby's Rockstar rocks up at Number 1 on the Official Irish Singles Chart for an eighth week|work=Official Charts}}</ref>
sections.text: "Rockstar" reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in its seventh week, for the chart issue dated June 13, 2020. It became DaBaby's first chart-topper and Roddy Ricch's second. It also became DaBaby's first number one and Ricch's second on Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs and Hot Rap Songs charts. Along with "The Box", Ricch became the first artist to achieve his first two number one singles in the same year since Ed Sheeran did it in 2017. Topping the chart for a second week, it became the first single to spend multiple weeks on top after a run in which five songs each spent a first and only week at the summit. It spent seven non-consecutive weeks atop the chart. "Rockstar" also spent six weeks at number one in both Australia and the United Kingdom, and eight weeks at the top in the Republic of Ireland.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
DaBaby teased a music video for "Rockstar" a week before its release, posting pictures on [[Instagram]] of the filming location.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/301676-dababy-teases-rockstar-music-video-with-roddy-ricch-you-ready-news|title=DaBaby Teases "Rockstar" Music Video With Roddy Ricch: "You Ready?"|work=HotNewHipHop|date=June 25, 2020 }}</ref> The Reel Goats-directed video was premiered on June 26, 2020, starring the two rappers hunting zombies in an open field.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2020/06/dababy-and-roddy-rich-rockstar-video|title=Watch DaBaby and Roddy Ricch's New "Rockstar" Video|work=Complex}}</ref> The seven-minute video also features a scene set to DaBaby's chorus and first verse to "Amazing Grace", which also is featured on [[Blame It on Baby|Blame It On Baby]] following by the credits playing his verse from the Black Lives Matter remix.<ref name="rs">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/dababy-roddy-ricch-rockstar-music-video-1021034/|title=DaBaby, Roddy Ricch Take on the Zombie Apocalypse in 'Rockstar' Video|magazine=Rolling Stone|date=June 26, 2020}}</ref>

In ''[[Rolling Stone]]'', Jon Blistein noted the video "boasts a distinctly cinematic feel" as the two rappers are heavily armed shooting a horde of zombies with "plenty of over-the-top action," that is "balanced by a refreshingly self-aware sequence" in which the two perform the song backed by a group of zombies dancing and playing instruments.<ref name="rs"/>
sections.text:
DaBaby teased a music video for "Rockstar" a week before its release, posting pictures on Instagram of the filming location. The Reel Goats-directed video was premiered on June 26, 2020, starring the two rappers hunting zombies in an open field. The seven-minute video also features a scene set to DaBaby's chorus and first verse to "Amazing Grace", which also is featured on Blame It On Baby following by the credits playing his verse from the Black Lives Matter remix.

In Rolling Stone, Jon Blistein noted the video "boasts a distinctly cinematic feel" as the two rappers are heavily armed shooting a horde of zombies with "plenty of over-the-top action," that is "balanced by a refreshingly self-aware sequence" in which the two perform the song backed by a group of zombies dancing and playing instruments.

sections.heading: Production
sections.wikitext: "Rockstar" was produced by North Carolina producer SethInTheKitchen, who also co-wrote the song.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Making Of DaBaby's "Rockstar" With SethInTheKitchen|url=https://genius.com/a/the-making-of-dababys-rockstar-with-sethinthekitchen|access-date=October 20, 2021|website=Genius|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine|title=SethInTheKitchen Tops Hot 100 Producers Chart, Thanks to DaBaby's 'Rockstar'|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/business/chart-beat/9404154/sethinthekitchen-tops-hot-100-producers-chart|access-date=October 20, 2021|magazine=Billboard|language=en}}</ref> The instrumental for "Rockstar" is a melodic [[Trap music|trap]] beat featuring a guitar loop created from [[Spectrasonics]]' Omnisphere.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sampling 101: The Ultimate Guide|url=https://racksstevenson.com/blogs/main-blog/sampling-101-the-ultimate-guide|access-date=October 20, 2021|website=Racks Stevenson Sample Library|language=en}}</ref> The drums consist of a two-step hi-hat pattern with assorted hat rolls, sampled claps, snares, and kicks. Its bassline features an [[Roland TR-808|808]].<ref>{{Citation|title=The Making Of DaBaby's "ROCKSTAR" With SethInTheKitchen {{!}} Deconstructed| date=July 7, 2020 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4VWMulVKL7Q|language=en|access-date=October 20, 2021}}</ref>
sections.text: "Rockstar" was produced by North Carolina producer SethInTheKitchen, who also co-wrote the song. The instrumental for "Rockstar" is a melodic trap beat featuring a guitar loop created from Spectrasonics' Omnisphere. The drums consist of a two-step hi-hat pattern with assorted hat rolls, sampled claps, snares, and kicks. Its bassline features an 808.

sections.heading: "Rockstar Black Lives Matter Remix"
sections.wikitext: On June 12, 2020, a remix of the song, titled "Rockstar Black Lives Matter Remix", was released. It joined many other [[protest song]]s that spoke out against [[police brutality]] in the wake of the [[killing of Breonna Taylor]] and [[murder of George Floyd]]. Jessica McKinney of ''[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]'' explained how on this version, DaBaby "discusses his multiple run-ins with the police, saying, 'Cops wanna pull me over, embarrass me/Abusin' power, you never knew me, thought I was arrogant/As a juvenile, police pulled their guns like they scared of me'{{-"}}, while Roddy Ricch "shares a similar experience, recalling a time the police stopped him at a gas station".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/music/a/j-mckinney/best-new-music-this-week-pop-smoke-lil-baby-rmr|title=Best New Music This Week: Pop Smoke, Lil Baby, RMR, and More|work=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]|last=McKinney|first=Jessica|date=June 12, 2020|access-date=June 20, 2020|archive-date=December 4, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201204023712/https://amp.www.complex.com/music/2020/06/best-new-music-this-week-pop-smoke-lil-baby-rmr|url-status=dead}}</ref> It later ended up on the deluxe version of ''Blame It On Baby'', which was released on August 4, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stream DaBaby's 'Blame It on Baby' Deluxe Album|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2020/08/dababy-blame-it-on-baby-deluxe|access-date=December 4, 2020|website=Complex|language=en}}</ref>
sections.text: On June 12, 2020, a remix of the song, titled "Rockstar Black Lives Matter Remix", was released. It joined many other protest songs that spoke out against police brutality in the wake of the killing of Breonna Taylor and murder of George Floyd. Jessica McKinney of Complex explained how on this version, DaBaby "discusses his multiple run-ins with the police, saying, 'Cops wanna pull me over, embarrass me/Abusin' power, you never knew me, thought I was arrogant/As a juvenile, police pulled their guns like they scared of me'{{-"}}, while Roddy Ricch "shares a similar experience, recalling a time the police stopped him at a gas station". It later ended up on the deluxe version of Blame It On Baby, which was released on August 4, 2020.

sections.heading: Live performances
sections.wikitext: DaBaby and Ricch performed the song live at the [[2020 BET Awards]]. The performance opened in a close-up shot of DaBaby on the ground with the knee of a police officer sitting on his neck — a recreation of [[George Floyd]]'s murder. He then appeared surrounded by protesters — channeling the nationwide protests against police brutality — and performing in front of burning police cars. Ricch joined him for his verse, standing atop a cop car.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/bet-awards-dababy-roddy-ricch-rockstar-george-floyd-1021647/|title=DaBaby Channels George Floyd for Powerful 'Rockstar' Performance at BET Awards|magazine=Rolling Stone|date=June 29, 2020}}</ref> The duo also performed the song at the [[63rd Annual Grammy Awards|Grammy Awards]] in 2021.
